oewn-01288228-s.learner: having or showing great dignity or a noble quality.
examples: The proud mountains rose high above the little town.

connotation.why: grants dignity where 'tall' or 'upright' would only describe

oewn-02349336-a.learner: of high quality, or doing very well.
examples: Such very superior dancing is not often seen
Mr. Gardiner was a sensible, gentlemanlike man, greatly superior to his sister, as well by nature as education.

oewn-00073044-s.learner: above being touched or moved by something, so that it does not affect you.
examples: He stood calm in the storm, superior to fear.

oewn-00796324-s.learner: not under the control or influence of something.
examples: The rich men acted as if they were superior to the law.

oewn-02358224-a.learner: written or printed a little above and to one side of another letter or number.
examples: In the word, the note number is printed as a small superior figure.

oewn-02357021-a.learner: moving around the sun on a path that is farther from the sun than the Earth's path.
examples: Mars is a superior planet, because it goes around the sun outside the Earth's path.

oewn-00304943-s.learner: of wind, sea, sky, or weather: seeming to show violent anger.
examples: Angry clouds gathered over the dark sea.

oewn-01177241-s.learner: badly swollen and sore, and hurting a lot.
examples: He had an angry red cut on his arm.

oewn-02336100-s.learner: putting all your strength and attention into something.
examples: They made a determined effort to finish the work before dark.

oewn-02137288-s.learner: fixed or decided, as if by someone with the power to decide.
examples: The date and place of the meeting are already determined.

oewn-01614867-a.learner: learned, found, or worked out, especially by looking into something carefully.
examples: The cause of the fire is not yet determined.

oewn-01467633-s.learner: having or showing warm, loving feelings.
examples: Poor Reynolds, she was always very fond of me.
She gave her little brother a fond smile.

oewn-01467366-s.learner: loving someone too much or in a foolish way, and letting them have whatever they want.
examples: The boy was spoiled by a fond mother who never said no.

connotation.why: calls the love excessive where 'loving' would not

oewn-02582341-s.learner: foolish or silly, because it is not likely to happen.
examples: He had fond hopes of getting rich overnight.

connotation.why: treats the hope as foolish where 'hopeful' would not

oewn-01984219-a.learner: keeping something in mind and paying attention to it.
examples: She was always aware of the needs of the people around her.
He was a difficult child who never did what he was told.

connotation.why: marks a person as a problem where 'strong-willed' would not

oewn-00446553-a.learner: not far away in place, time, amount, or situation.
examples: She was not near enough to hear any of their discourse
We will meet again in the near future.

oewn-00454916-s.learner: in a close or deep relationship with someone.
examples: there is now in the room a near relation to my patroness.

oewn-01578155-s.learner: very like the real thing, without being it.
examples: Her dress was made of near silk that looked almost real.
The rider got onto the horse from its near side.

oewn-00756368-s.learner: making people feel sorry for someone while also looking down on them.
examples: The old man looked silly, chasing a girl who only laughed at him.

connotation.why: adds scorn where 'sad' would only ask for pity

oewn-00438938-s.learner: confused and unable to think clearly from being hit again and again, or as if you had been.
examples: The blow knocked him silly.

oewn-00090922-s.learner: very unpleasant and not at all nice.
examples: It rained all day, and the weather was dreadful.
